walkthroughs.body_html:
Systematic Approach To Problem Solving — a core area of A-Level Computer Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Systematic Approach To Problem Solving brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Systematic Approach To Problem Solving.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Hoare's quicksort algorithm was published in:
Binary search time complexity (on sorted array):
options: O(log n)
O(n)

mcqs.q: What is the difference between OR and XOR?
options: Copy code from any unrelated class.
They are the same gate with different names.
OR is true when at least one input is true; XOR is true when exactly one input is true.
OR is for numbers, XOR is for letters.

mcqs.q: What does inheritance allow a subclass to do?
options: Copy code from any unrelated class.
Reuse and extend the attributes and methods of its superclass.
It is impossible to break.
Replace the superclass entirely.

mcqs.q: What is the main advantage of asymmetric encryption?
options: Secure key exchange without sharing a secret in advance.
Copy code from any unrelated class.
It is faster than symmetric encryption.
It is impossible to break.
